mainTopic: Writing a גט and other documents in advance: the reasons for leaving the names and date blank, why every גט needs a date, and the ruling like רבי אלעזר
overview: The גמרא first settles a contradiction: the משנה seems to quote רבי אלעזר both ways, and the answer is that two תנאים reported his view differently. It then asks why a סופר who writes a גט in advance must leave the names and date blank. חזקיה says the reason is to prevent fights at home, following רבי מאיר. אבימי says the reason is to help עגונות, and there are two versions of how that works: one following רבי מאיר and one following רבי אלעזר. Next the גמרא asks why a גט from אירוסין needs a date, since the 'produce' reason does not apply to a betrothed woman. רב עמרם answers with עולא's reason: the date protects the child, so people will not say her גט came before her son. Finally, רב rules like רבי אלעזר, who allows other documents to be written in advance. The גמרא shows that 'looking like a lie' does not invalidate ordinary documents, using רבי מאיר's garbage-גט and רבי יוחנן's ruling about a repaid loan document.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two statements of רבי אלעזר in the same משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: one statement of רבי אלעזר contradicts another statement of רבי אלעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had just said that the first part of the משנה follows רבי אלעזר. Now it asks how that can be, since the last part of the משנה quotes רבי אלעזר saying the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on the first part of the משנה, רבי אלעזר would let a סופר write the standard text of a גט ahead of time. But at the end of the משנה, רבי אלעזר says by name that this is not allowed. The same תנא cannot hold both views.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty; something that does not fit
'Against'. Used to set one statement against another

phrases.english: It is difficult: Rabbi Elazar against Rabbi Elazar!
phrases.notes: One view is what we figured out from the first part of the משנה. The other is what רבי אלעזר says by name at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim (before this section) that the first part of the משנה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first part of the משנה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last part of the משנה quotes רבי אלעזר directly with the opposite ruling, so the same תנא cannot also be behind the first part.

steps.title: Two תנאים report רבי אלעזר's view differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two different תנאים disagreed about what רבי אלעזר actually held.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי אלעזר's opinion was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. רבי אלעזר did not contradict himself. Two different תנאים passed down his view in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה follows one תנא's report of רבי אלעזר's opinion. The last part follows a different תנא's report. So the disagreement is about what רבי אלעזר said, not a contradiction inside his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים (teachers of the משנה period)
According to; in the opinion of

steps.whatToRemember: When the same תנא seems to hold two opposite views, the גמרא can answer that two later תנאים reported his opinion differently.

phrases.english: There are two Tannaim, and they disagree about the view of Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among later sources about what one authority held (תרי תנאי אליבא ד־)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed there was only one report of רבי אלעזר's view, so the two parts of the משנה clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two parts of the משנה reflect two different reports of רבי אלעזר's view.

steps.title: First reason for the rule: to prevent a quarrel
steps.stepSummary: רבי שבתי, quoting חזקיה, says the rule of leaving blank spaces was made to prevent fights, and that it follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שבתי said in the name of חזקיה: the rule was made because of quarrels. It follows רבי מאיר, who says that the witnesses who sign the גט are what make the divorce happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rule in the משנה that a סופר must leave the names and date blank, and offers a first reason for it. This line states the reason and names the תנא it follows. The next step explains how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds עדי חתימה כרתי: the signing witnesses make the גט work. So only the signing has to be done for this particular woman (לשמה), not the writing. That means the blank spaces cannot be required by the basic law. They must be a rule the חכמים added for another reason, namely preventing fights.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarrel or fight
The witnesses who sign the גט
'Cut', meaning they make the divorce take effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר here. רבי מאיר says the SIGNING witnesses make the divorce. That is why, for him, the writing does not need to be done for this woman at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shabbetai said in the name of Ḥizkiyya:
It is because of a quarrel;
and it follows Rabbi Meir,
who says: the signing witnesses make the divorce take effect,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שַׁבְּתַי אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: מִשּׁוּם קְטָטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the reason behind the rule in the משנה, after the contradiction about רבי אלעזר was settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule of leaving blank spaces is meant to prevent a quarrel, and it follows רבי מאיר (עדי חתימה כרתי).

steps.title: How writing the names could start a fight
steps.stepSummary: By the basic law even the names and date (תורף) could be written in advance. But a wife who hears a סופר writing a גט with her name might think her husband ordered it, and a fight would break out.
steps.simpleTranslation: By the basic law, the סופר should be allowed to write even the תורף ahead of time. But sometimes a wife hears the סופר writing it, thinks her husband told him to, and a fight starts between them.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues חזקיה's explanation. It shows how pre-writing the names could cause a quarrel, and why the חכמים banned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, nothing in the writing has to be done for this woman, so even the תורף could be written early. The ban exists only because a wife might overhear the סופר writing a גט with her and her husband's names. She would wrongly think her husband wants to divorce her, and that would cause a fight. So the blank spaces are a rule to keep peace in the home, not a basic legal need.

keyTerms.meaning: The essential, personal part of the גט: the names of husband and wife, and the date
By the basic law; strictly speaking
Scribe
Sometimes

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that for רבי מאיר the blank spaces are a rule of the חכמים, made to prevent fights at home. They are not a rule about what makes a גט valid.

phrases.aramaic: וּבְדִין הוּא דַּאֲפִילּוּ תּוֹרֶף נָמֵי לִכְתּוֹב;
phrases.english: By right, he should be allowed to write even the essential part as well;

phrases.aramaic: וְזִמְנִין דְּשָׁמְעָה לֵיהּ לְסוֹפֵר דְּקָא כָתֵיב,
phrases.english: but sometimes she hears the scribe as he is writing,
and she thinks that he (her husband) told him to,
and she will have a quarrel with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִין הוּא דַּאֲפִילּוּ תּוֹרֶף נָמֵי לִכְתּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the 'quarrel' reason from step 3 works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By the basic law even the תורף could be written in advance. It was banned so that a wife who overhears will not think her husband ordered a גט and start a fight.

steps.title: Second reason: to help deserted wives
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, gives a different reason for the rule: helping עגונות. There are two versions of which תנא this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: the rule was made to help עגונות. Some say this follows רבי מאיר, and some say it follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different reason for the rule and reports two opinions about which תנא it follows. This sets up the next part, where the גמרא will explain how the reason works under each view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new reason, separate from חזקיה's. The rule is meant to protect women who could be left stuck in their marriage. This line does not yet explain how the rule helps them. It only says that people disagreed about whether the reason fits רבי מאיר or רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule made to help עגונות, women stuck in their marriage who cannot remarry

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said in the name of Avimi:
It is because of a remedy for deserted wives;
some say it follows Rabbi Meir,
and some say it follows Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲבִימִי: מִשּׁוּם תַּקָּנַת עֲגוּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason for the same rule, instead of חזקיה's 'quarrel' reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule was made to help עגונות. Some say this follows רבי מאיר and some say רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: First version: the rule follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the signing witnesses make the גט work. So by strict law even the names and date could be written ahead of time. The חכמים still required blank spaces so a husband in an angry moment would not have a ready גט to throw at his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this follows רבי מאיר, who said the signing witnesses make the divorce happen. By strict law, even the main part (names and date) could be written ahead of time. But sometimes the husband has a fight with his wife. He gets angry, throws the גט to her, and abandons her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first version of רב חסדא's עגונה reason. In this version the rule of leaving blank spaces follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the signatures are what make the גט work, so writing the תורף early would not make the גט invalid. The rule is only a protection. If a fully written גט were sitting ready, an angry husband could use it at once. Making him wait for the סופר gives him time to cool down.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses who sign the גט
They 'cut' the marriage, meaning they make the divorce take effect
The main personal part of the גט: names and date
A quarrel or fight
Abandons her, leaving her in a bad, stuck situation

phrases.english: Some say it follows Rabbi Meir –
who said: the signing witnesses make the divorce take effect,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְדִין הוּא דַּאֲפִילּוּ תּוֹרֶף נָמֵי לִכְתּוֹב;
phrases.english: and by strict law even the main part could also be written in advance;
but sometimes he has a quarrel with her,
and he gets angry at her and throws it to her,
and he deserts her and leaves her that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first of the two versions mentioned in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבי מאיר, the תורף could be written in advance by strict law. The חכמים forbade it so an angry husband would not have a ready גט to use on impulse.

steps.title: Second version: the rule follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אלעזר, the witnesses who see the handing-over make the גט work. So by strict law even the standard text should not be written in advance. The חכמים allowed it so a traveling husband could get a גט quickly and not leave his wife an עגונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say this follows רבי אלעזר, who said the witnesses to the handing-over make the divorce happen. By strict law, even the standard text should not be written in advance. But sometimes the husband needs to travel overseas and cannot find a סופר. He would leave her and go, and she would be stuck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second version of the עגונה reason. In this version the rule follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the problem is the opposite of step 6. By strict law nothing should be written early, not even the טופס. The חכמים relaxed this and allowed the טופס to be pre-written. That way a husband in a rush could finish a גט quickly instead of leaving his wife an עגונה.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses who watch the גט being handed to the wife
The standard, general text of the גט that is the same for everyone
A faraway land overseas
A scribe (סופר)

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions point in opposite directions. In the רבי מאיר version, the rule is a stricter limit on what may be written early. In the רבי אלעזר version, the rule is a leniency that allows the טופס to be written early.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions use the same עגונה reason. For רבי מאיר it explains why the תורף may NOT be written early. For רבי אלעזר it explains why the טופס MAY be written early.

phrases.english: Some say it follows Rabbi Elazar –
who said: the witnesses to the handing-over make the divorce take effect,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְדִין הוּא דַּאֲפִילּוּ טוֹפֶס נָמֵי לָא לִכְתּוֹב;
phrases.english: and by strict law even the standard text should not be written in advance;
but sometimes he needs to travel overseas
and he does not find a scribe,
so he leaves her and goes,
and he deserts her and leaves her stuck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second version, which is the opposite of step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבי אלעזר, the טופס should not be written in advance by strict law. The חכמים allowed it so a traveling husband would not leave his wife an עגונה.

steps.title: The space for the date applies to every divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's words 'and a space for the date.' It notes that the משנה makes no distinction: the rule applies whether the divorce ends a marriage (נישואין) or a betrothal (אירוסין).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a space for the date': the תנא teaches it without any exceptions. It makes no difference whether the divorce is from full marriage or from betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: the space for the date. It points out that the משנה says this about every divorce. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By stressing that the משנה draws no line, the גמרא prepares a problem. If a date is required even for a divorce from אירוסין, the reasons for dating a גט must also apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: The space left for the date
He teaches it as a flat rule, with no exceptions
Full marriage, after the חופה
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage before living together

phrases.english: 'And a space for the date':
he teaches it without any exceptions;
no difference if it is from full marriage,
and no difference if it is from betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the reason for blank spaces and turns to the משנה's rule about the date
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה requires a space for the date in every גט, whether from נישואין or from אירוסין.

steps.title: Why a date makes sense for a divorce from full marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a 'בשלמא' challenge. For a divorce from נישואין, both reasons for dating a גט apply: the בת אחותו concern and the פירות concern. This sets up the coming question about אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a divorce from full marriage. Whether you follow the one who says the date is needed because of 'his sister's daughter,' or the one who says it is needed because of the produce, the reason applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants that dating a גט makes sense after full marriage. It is setting up a challenge: what about a divorce from אירוסין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier reasons for dating a גט fit a married couple. The בת אחותו reason prevents a husband from covering for his wife if she sinned. The פירות reason fixes from when her property's produce belongs to her again. The word בשלמא signals that the next line will ask how these reasons fit אירוסין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense that…', which opens a challenge
His sister's daughter, one of the reasons for dating a גט
Produce, meaning the income from the wife's property

phrases.english: It makes sense for a divorce from full marriage;

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם בַּת אֲחוֹתוֹ – אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: both according to the one who says it is because of his sister's daughter, the reason applies,
phrases.notes: This and the 'produce' reason are two reasons given earlier in the מסכתא for why a גט must be dated.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם פֵּירֵי – אִיכָּא;
phrases.english: and according to the one who says it is because of the produce, the reason applies;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8's point that the date applies to all divorces, and begins the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of a date even for a divorce from אירוסין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known reasons for dating a גט clearly apply after נישואין. The unstated implication is that they may not apply after אירוסין, which the next lines will press.

steps.title: The produce reason does not fit a betrothed woman
steps.stepSummary: The בת אחותו reason works for אירוסין, but the פירות reason does not, because an ארוסה has no produce for her husband to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a divorce from betrothal: the בת אחותו reason still works there. But the produce reason? Does a betrothed woman have produce?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in Step 9. One reason for dating a גט works for a betrothed woman, but the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dating the גט because of בת אחותו still makes sense, since a betrothed woman's unfaithfulness is already a serious sin. But a husband only gets rights to his wife's produce after נישואין. So the פירות reason gives no need to date a גט from אירוסין, yet the משנה requires a date for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A betrothed woman
Produce or profits from the wife's property
His sister's daughter (the reason from earlier in the סוגיא)

phrases.english: But from betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם בַּת אֲחוֹתוֹ – אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: granted, according to the one who says it is because of his sister's daughter, that concern exists;
phrases.notes: This is the earlier reason: the date stops a husband from shielding his wife from punishment if she was unfaithful, by claiming an undated גט came first.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says it is because of produce,
does a betrothed woman have produce?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא challenge set up in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פירות reason for dating a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires a date even for a גט from אירוסין, but the produce reason does not exist there.

steps.title: עולא's reason: protecting the child
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם explains that the date protects the child. Without it, people might think the גט came before the baby, making the child look like a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: I heard from עולא that the date is for the child's sake, and I did not understand it. Then I heard the ברייתא: if a man says 'write a גט for my betrothed, and I will divorce her with it after I marry her,' it is not a גט. עולא explained: this is a גזירה, so people will not say her גט came before her son. Here too, the date is required so people will not say her גט came before her son.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם gives a third reason for dating a גט, תקנת ולד, which also works for a betrothed woman. He explains it using a ברייתא and עולא's reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט written during אירוסין might be given only after the couple marries and has a child. If people saw the writing date, they might think she was already divorced when the child was conceived and wrongly suspect the child. So the date must be written when the גט is actually prepared and given, which answers the question in Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule made to protect the child
A rabbinic safeguard decree
Her גט came before her son

steps.whatToRemember: A גט is dated for three reasons: בת אחותו, פירות, and תקנת ולד. The child reason explains why even a גט from אירוסין needs a date.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said:
I heard this matter from Ulla,
who said it is for the benefit of the child,
phrases.notes: He means the reason a גט must be dated.

phrases.english: and I did not know what it was.
Once I heard what was taught:
One who says: 'Write a bill of divorce for my betrothed,
for when I marry her I will divorce her' — it is not a valid bill of divorce.
And Ulla said: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ: גִּיטָּהּ קוֹדֵם לִבְנָהּ.
phrases.english: A decree, lest people say: her bill of divorce came before her son.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי – גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ: גִּיטָּהּ קוֹדֵם לִבְנָהּ.
phrases.english: Here too, it is a decree lest people say: her bill of divorce came before her son.
phrases.notes: Here he means the date in a גט from אירוסין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם הָא מִילְּתָא שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10 with a reason that applies even to אירוסין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the date that also applies to a betrothed woman
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reasons for dating were בת אחותו and פירות, and פירות does not apply to an ארוסה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The date also protects the child from looking like he was conceived after the גט was given.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Through a long chain of teachers, רב rules like רבי אלעזר and praises him as the most fortunate of the Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through a chain of teachers, רב said: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר. רב called רבי אלעזר 'the most fortunate of the Sages.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר's view in the משנה. רבי אלעזר allows document forms to be written ahead of time for all documents except a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling comes through five links: רבי זירא, רבי אבא בר שילא, רב המנונא סבא, רב אדא בר אהבה, and רב. רב's praise shows how strongly he backed this view. The next step asks how far this ruling reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows רבי אלעזר
The most fortunate (praiseworthy) of the Sages

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר שֵׁילָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Abba bar Sheila said
that Rav Hamnuna the Elder said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.
Rav called out about Rabbi Elazar:
The most fortunate of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the date discussion to a practical ruling on the משנה's argument.

steps.title: Does the ruling apply to other documents too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ruling like רבי אלעזר covers other documents. A judges' approval written before the witnesses confirmed their signatures is invalid because it looks like a lie, so writing other documents early should look like a lie too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even for other documents too?! But רב פפי said in the name of רבא: a judges' approval written before witnesses confirmed their signatures is invalid. So it looks like a lie. Here too it looks like a lie!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how far the ruling in Step 12 reaches. It uses a rule from רבא about a court approval written too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rules that judges may not write their approval of a document before the witnesses testify about their signatures. Even if the testimony comes later, the approval states something that was not yet true when written. The גמרא argues that documents prepared ahead of time have the same problem of looking false.

keyTerms.meaning: Other legal documents (not a גט)
The judges' approval of a document
It looks like a lie
Invalid

phrases.english: And even with other documents too?!
But didn't Rav Pappi say in the name of Rava:
This approval of the judges,
phrases.notes: This is the note judges add to a document saying they checked the witnesses' signatures.

phrases.aramaic: דְּמִיכַּתְבָה מִקַּמֵּי דְּלִיסָהֲדֵי סָהֲדִי אַחֲתִימַת יְדַיְיהוּ – פְּסוּלָה;
phrases.english: that was written before the witnesses testified about their signatures, is invalid;
evidently, it looks like a lie;
here too, it looks like a lie!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the ruling in Step 12 extends.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the ruling like רבי אלעזר to other documents
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A judges' approval written before the testimony is invalid because it looks false. A document written ahead of time should look false in the same way.

steps.title: The 'looks like a lie' idea is rejected using רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the claim that early-written documents are invalid because they look false. It brings רב נחמן's report that, according to רבי מאיר, even a גט found in the garbage is valid once it is signed and given.
steps.simpleTranslation: That idea is not accepted, because of what רב נחמן said. רבי מאיר used to say: even if a husband found a גט in the garbage, had it signed, and gave it to his wife, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the challenge from Step 13. It shows that a document written long before it is used can still be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט found in the garbage was obviously written without this couple in mind. Still, רבי מאיר says it is valid once it is signed and handed over. So, at least for רבי מאיר, the early writing does not create a 'lie' problem at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not accepted (the earlier statement is rejected)
Garbage heap
He had it signed (by witnesses)
Valid

phrases.english: And that idea is not accepted, because of Rav Nachman's statement:
phrases.notes: 'That idea' is the claim from the last step that any document written early looks like a lie.

phrases.english: For Rav Nachman said:
Rabbi Meir would say:
Even if he found it in the garbage,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a written גט that has no signatures yet. For רבי מאיר, the signing witnesses are what make the גט work.

phrases.english: had it signed and gave it to her, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'looks like a lie' challenge raised in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The general claim that every document written in advance is invalid because it looks false.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר validates a גט that was written with no connection to this couple. This shows that early writing is not treated as a lie.

steps.title: The חכמים argue only about a גט, not other documents
steps.stepSummary: Even the חכמים who disagree with רבי מאיר do so only for a גט, because a גט must be written לשמה. For all other documents, they agree that early writing is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר only about a woman's גט, because it must be written for her sake. For other documents, they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes sure the proof works for everyone, not just רבי מאיר. The חכמים' disagreement is limited to a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים reject the garbage-גט only because of a special rule for a גט: it must be written לשמה, for this specific woman. That reason has nothing to do with 'looking like a lie.' So for ordinary documents, which have no לשמה requirement, everyone agrees that early writing is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים (the majority of Sages)
Women's bills of divorce
Writing done specifically for her (this woman)
Other documents (loans, sales, and so on)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים reject the garbage-גט because it 'looks like a lie.' Their only reason is the special לשמה rule, which applies to a גט alone.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: And even the Rabbis do not disagree with Rabbi Meir
except regarding women's bills of divorce,
because there we require writing for her sake,
but regarding other documents, they do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends Step 14's rejection so that it holds even according to the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that ordinary documents written in advance are valid. The only dispute is about a גט, because of לשמה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a repaid loan document cannot be reused
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from רבי יוחנן. A loan document that was used and then paid off cannot be used again for a new loan, because its שעבוד was already cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone borrowed with a document and then paid it back, he cannot borrow again with that same document, because its lien was already forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the claim that early writing is not a 'lie' problem. This step gives רבי יוחנן's ruling, and the next step draws the inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses signed the document for the first loan. Once that loan is repaid, the lien it created is finished. Reusing the document for a second loan fails, and רבי יוחנן gives a specific reason for that.

keyTerms.meaning: A written document (here, a loan document)
He paid it back
Lien: the legal claim on the borrower's property that the document creates
Was forgiven or cancelled

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A document with which one borrowed and then repaid,
he may not go back and borrow with it again,
since its lien has already been forgiven.
phrases.notes: The witnesses signed only for the first loan. Once it was paid, that signed claim was finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source supporting the claim in Step 15 that ordinary documents are not invalid because they look like a lie.
steps.raayaObject: Writing ordinary documents in advance is not a 'looks like a lie' problem.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a repaid loan document cannot be reused because its שעבוד was forgiven.

steps.title: The only problem is the lost lien, not 'looking like a lie'
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's wording, the גמרא infers that the only reason the document cannot be reused is the cancelled שעבוד. We are not worried about it looking like a lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that its lien was forgiven. But because of 'looking like a lie,' we are not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into the reason רבי יוחנן gave and draws the final point. 'Looking like a lie' is not a concern for documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reused document was clearly written before the second loan, so it 'looks false' about that loan. If that were a problem, רבי יוחנן could have said so. Instead he gave only the reason of the cancelled lien, which shows that writing in advance by itself is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is
Falsehood, 'looking like a lie'
We are not concerned

steps.whatToRemember: Ordinary documents may be written before the event they record. 'Looking like a lie' (שיקרא) does not invalidate them. A גט is different only because it needs לשמה, and a repaid loan document fails only because its שעבוד is gone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the challenge from Step 13. The ruling like רבי אלעזר is therefore not threatened by any general 'early writing is a lie' concern.

phrases.english: The reason is that its lien was forgiven,
but because of the appearance of falsehood, we are not concerned.
phrases.notes: The 'falsehood' is that the document was written before the second loan ever happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּנִמְחַל שִׁעְבּוּדוֹ, אֲבָל מִשּׁוּם שִׁיקְרָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from רבי יוחנן's wording in Step 16, completing the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no concern of שיקרא for documents written in advance. Such documents are invalid only for other reasons, like a cancelled שעבוד or, for a גט, the requirement of לשמה.
